title: I made these two spells today entirely through vibe coding, and I’m really happy with how they turned out!
author: TheKamiBoy
selftext: I’m planning to add hundreds of different spells to Ninefir, the game I’m developing, and GPT-6 Sol has been a great option for creating this kind of animation.

comments.author: YYY003003
comments.body: Pretty pretty cool. How did you make the spell animations?

replies.author: TheKamiBoy
replies.body: Thank you so much! The character is animated by hand, but the spell sprites were made entirely through vibe coding. I gave GPT the initial idea and kept asking it to refine the result until we got to this.

comments.author: joeban1
comments.body:
Looks awesome. Did it create it with its imagegen skill and render spritesheets? 

Or is this just another js animation

replies.author: TheKamiBoy
replies.body:
For the spells specifically, GPT first uses ImageGen to create a visual reference based on my idea, then uses that reference as a guide to recreate and animate the effect in Aseprite. I keep iterating with it until the result fits the game.

The character itself is different: I drew and animated the base character by hand. The outfit did involve AI generation, but since I already had the complete character base and animations, the AI basically generated the clothing on top of that existing base. I then manually fixed the imperfections and refined everything so it matched the character and the game’s art style.

replies.author: FamiliarEstimate6267
replies.body: How’d u get it to use asprite

replies.author: joeban1
replies.body: and how does it operate aseprite? via an mcp?

replies.author: TheKamiBoy
replies.body: I have the PixelLab plugin installed in Aseprite. It already has its own AI that can generate pixel art. So I ask Codex to create pixel art for me using Aseprite. Sometimes it does it directly, and other times it can use PixelLab.

replies.author: TheKamiBoy
replies.body: But its no MCP. Its runs directly. I don't know how it exactly works. But I call for a aseprite file, then it gaves me aseprite!

comments.author: jaykrown
comments.body: This is the way. You're taking a platform you've built and are deliberately adding value in a specific way rather than just "one shotting" garbage. I really like how the orbs you fire disappear one by one as you use them. Incrementally building like this in a modular way clearly shows you know what you're doing.

replies.author: TheKamiBoy
replies.body: Thank you! I’ve really been taking full advantage of AI’s potential to create things the way I’ve always dreamed of. It’s definitely not a one-shot process. There’s a huge amount of refinement involved, as well as a lot of manual work in some parts of the game, although these particular spells were made entirely through vibe coding.

replies.author: jaykrown
replies.body: Indeed it's good to be transparent about that. What you're doing is a great way to build. Even if you are vibe coding the spells, you're doing so in a system that you created to make it such that you can add them in that way. Architecting the system to make that easy is what is most valuable.
